What comes up in Chipping Norton

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. This sets out the typical case here rather than anything about a given address.

House and pool in one scope

Common on the larger Chipping Norton lots, where the rear yard carries as much work as the house does.

How it is handled
Taken down separately so the streams stay apart, with the pool shell broken out and the void backfilled and compacted in layers.
What does it
Midi excavator with a grapple and a hammer, tippers for the rubble and clean fill back in.

Dig on soft low lying ground

Nearer the river, where the ground holds water and a face will not stand on its own.

How it is handled
Battered back or supported rather than left vertical, with dewatering where the condition calls for it.
What does it
Excavator with pumps on site and a batter designed for the ground.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Chipping Norton

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Riverside and low lying ground in parts Which affects drainage, how an excavation holds up and what material is suitable for reuse.
  • Large blocks with room to work Generous frontages on much of the older stock, so access is rarely the binding constraint.
  • Pools and rear yard structures Common on the larger lots, and each is a separate waste stream.
  • Former industrial land nearby Which makes fill of unknown origin worth testing rather than assuming on sites with a history.

Chipping Norton streets generally take a tipper comfortably and many will take a truck and dog. Nearer the river the ground can be soft after rain, which affects where plant can track and how material is loaded more than it affects the demolition.

Chipping Norton questions

What people ask before we start

Does low lying ground change an excavation?
Yes. Where the water table is close, an open excavation does not stay dry, so dewatering and support are planned rather than discovered once the hole is open. It also affects what the material is suitable for if it is being reused.
Can the pool come out at the same time as the house?
Yes, and it is more efficient that way. The shell is broken out and removed, then the void is backfilled with material suitable for whatever is going on top and compacted in layers.
Do you work in the new growth estates as well as the older suburbs?
Yes, and they are different jobs. In Oran Park, Leppington and Box Hill the work is site cut, levelling and fill because there was little standing to begin with. In Camden and Campbelltown it is demolition on stock that goes back decades.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
